scope: Second-order deductions from the current EdgeBench v1 theory and public runtime for science-specific experiment design. These are Frontier-Science proposals, not additional EdgeBench empirical results.
source_facts: The theory requires average score-unit granularity error to vanish and notes that coarse score units can preserve jumps and variance.
The benchmark-level derivation treats different task environments as non-interacting and requires aligned task midpoints and concentrated task speeds.
The theory assumes a stable attainable support and approximately linear search-effort supply; it lists characteristic cycles and batch feedback as reasons a single log-time coordinate can fail.
The paper reports decreasing fit error as task count grows, but the paper and public source do not report permutation- or subsample-distributions for that task-count curve.
The official public Codex configuration gives each listed task an independent 12-hour default budget and staggers launches by 600 seconds; it is not a shared scientific portfolio allocation protocol.
The public harness supports asynchronous judging, but the released benchmark does not report experiments on drifting instruments, consumptive samples or irreversible interventions.

frontier_science_experiments.design: Replay identical raw physical outcomes under preregistered coarse, canonical and fine score partitions; refit under random and lineage-blocked task accumulation orders and subsamples.
Randomize related, unrelated and misleading source tasks before an answer-disjoint procedural target; compare cold, artifact-only, raw-evidence, audited-notebook and full-state starts.

Allocate one shared token, wall, instrument, oracle and confirmation budget across blinded signal, null, misspecified and multifidelity projects; compare equal, random, cost-aware VOI and agent policies.

Inject calibration drift, batch changes, sample depletion, irreversible interventions and randomized result latency into server-side world state; require state-compatible observation lineage and fresh-batch confirmation.

claim_boundary: No new EdgeBench numerical result is claimed.
The proposed stress tests are deductions from explicit assumptions and limits, not experiments reported by the EdgeBench authors.
Until these tests are run, Frontier-Science should not claim invariance of a scaling law, cross-task scientific meta-learning, portfolio-level autonomy or laboratory-state competence.
